activities.title: Count the words
parentPrompts: Say a short sentence, like "I love my family." Say it again slowly and put down one block for each word.
Count the blocks together. Ask: "How many words did we say?"
Let them make up a sentence about home. Say it back, one word at a time, and place the blocks.
Try a longer sentence and see if they notice it has more blocks.

activities.title: Put two words together
materials: pictures or objects for words like bedroom, cupcake, sunflower, toothbrush
parentPrompts: Show a picture of a bed and a room. Say: "bed... room. Put them together: bedroom!"
Try cup + cake, sun + flower, tooth + brush.
Take one part away: "Say bedroom. Now say it without bed." Use pictures or hand signals to help.
Look for compound words around the house and say them in two parts.

activities.title: Letters in family names
parentPrompts: Write the name of each family member or pet on a card, in big letters.
Point to the first letter of each name and say its sound. Ask: "What is the first letter in Grandma?"
Find objects around the house that begin with the same sound as each name.
Ask: "Whose name starts like yours?"

activities.title: Rhymes around the house
materials: a few household objects like a cup, a bed, a mug, and a chair
parentPrompts: Hold up an object and say its name. Ask: "What rhymes with cup?" Accept silly words too: "pup, tup, lup."
Try bed/red, mug/hug, chair/bear. Notice the matching end sounds.
Say three words and ask which one does not rhyme, like "bed, red, dog."
Take turns making up rhymes for things in the room.

activities.title: Read about families
materials: a picture book about families or homes
parentPrompts: Read the book together. Look for the different people and homes in the pictures.
Ask: "Who lives in this family? How is this family like ours? How is it different?"
Remind them that families come in many shapes and sizes, and all are good.
Ask them to tell you who is in their family and what they like to do together.

activities.title: Count things at home
parentPrompts: Walk through a room and count things together: chairs, windows, doors, pillows. Keep it to 10 or fewer.
Touch each thing once as you count. Ask: "How many?" and say the last number again.
Let them pick something to count and tell you how many.
Make it a game: "Can you find 4 things that are red?"

activities.title: Shape hunt
parentPrompts: Name the shapes first: circle, square, triangle, rectangle. Draw one of each.
Walk around the house looking for those shapes in doors, plates, windows, and books.
Ask: "What shape is this?" Turn an object upside down or sideways and ask again. A triangle is still a triangle.
Draw the shapes you found on a list.

activities.title: Build a shape house
materials: blocks, or paper shapes cut from construction paper
parentPrompts: Build a house with blocks, or glue paper shapes onto a page: a square for the house, a triangle for the roof.
Name each shape as you place it. Ask: "What shape should the door be?"
Try making a different building: a tall tower or a long wall.
Ask them to tell you what each shape is for.

activities.title: Where is it?
parentPrompts: Show the toy and place it on, under, next to, and behind the box. Say each position word as you go.
Hide the toy and give clues: "It is under something soft." Let them look.
Switch: they hide the toy and give you clues using position words.
Ask: "Where is the toy now?" and have them answer in a sentence.

activities.title: Favorite fruit graph
materials: a ruler or straight edge, optional
parentPrompts: Draw three columns on the paper with a picture of an apple, a banana, and an orange at the top.
Ask each family member (or stuffed animal) which fruit they like best, and let your child add a sticker or drawing in that column.
Count each column. Ask: "Which has the most? Which has the fewest?"
Ask what you could do with this information, like buying more of the favorite.

activities.title: Draw my home
parentPrompts: Ask them to draw the outside of their home, or any place they like to be.
Add details together: "What else is at your house? Who is inside?"
Ask them to tell you about their drawing, and write a sentence they say at the bottom.
Hang it up for everyone to see.

activities.title: Cardboard box house
parentPrompts: An adult should cut a door and windows. Little hands can decorate with crayons or paint.
Ask: "What rooms does our home have? What goes in each room?"
Use it for pretend play with toy people or animals.
Talk about how people make a place feel like home.

activities.title: Family paper bag puppets
parentPrompts: Decorate a paper bag as a person or pet, with a face, hair, and clothes.
Make one for each member of your family, or just a few.
Put on a little show: "Let the puppets say hello."
Ask: "What does this puppet like to do? What does it say?"

activities.title: Playdough dinner
materials: a plate and a spoon for pretend play
parentPrompts: Roll, pinch, and flatten playdough to make pretend food: a pizza, noodles, a cake.
Set the table for your family and pretend to serve a meal.
Ask: "What is your favorite food at home?"
Count the pieces of food on each plate.

subject: arts
title: Make a sign for my room

activities.title: Make a sign for my room
materials: a sheet of cardstock or paper
parentPrompts: Write their name in big letters on the sign, or help them write it themselves.
Point to each letter and say it. Let them decorate around the name.
Hang it on their door or wall.
Ask them to tell you why they like their name.
